Corposant creates a special buff card called "pilot". they are 0 cost derived cards whose main effect is to give a decent amount of shield - however, their discard effect is, to give you some strength and tentacle damage. 
This is your damage ramp mechanic - this is what allows your damage to get higher as the battle goes on.
She *also* has a 4 cost card, which has the aftershock effect of returning itself to your hand - this is done in order to repeatedly proc it's "prepare" effect, reducing it's arithmetica cost by 1 every time it gets discarded.

Meanwhile, her most typical partner is Aurita. Aurita has these little damaging 0 cost cards called "gland division", which are something you want to have in your discard pile, because her ult consumes them for extra damage instances. Each gland division has a discard effect that gives aurita some Aliemus, while the main effect deals some damage and places an *additional* gland division into the discard pile, meaning, that it doubles up every time you play it. 

Now, what happens when you play discard?
You draw a lot of cards, then you play all gland divisions, then you discard your cards, then you either get extra gland divisions, or you try to get something else set up - ideally you'd want to discard again. There's a few reasons, but in the end it's just to cycle through your deck faster and making Corposant's 4 cost cheaper. 
Whenever you have both Corposant's and Aurita's ult charged, the setup from earlier pays off - from discarding all your Pilots, you have a lot of tentacle damage and strength, and from using your gland divisions, you have a lot of those in your discard pile, which add up to *big boy aurita ult damage*
